evidence_snippets: Use of Hib conjugate vaccines has led to dramatic declines of >90% in invasive Hib disease in the countries which have included these vaccines in national immunization programmes.

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies of the clinical effectiveness of Hib vaccines against meningitis, pneumonia and other forms of invasive Hib disease have demonstrated that Hib vaccine effectively protects against these diseases.

Major declines in levels of nasopharyngeal Hib colonization have also been observed following introduction of Hib conjugate vaccines. This has led to substantially greater reduction in disease incidence than can be directly attributed to the effects of the vaccine, suggesting that widespread use of the vaccine has resulted in the induction of herd protection.
Data from 6 cohort studies suggests that starting vaccination at an older age may lead to higher vaccine effectiveness against invasive Hib disease.

Available data suggest that after 5 years of use of Hib conjugate vaccines, using a 3p+0 schedule, a sustained reduction in meningitis in young children has occurred in a number of developing countries.

A recent evaluation from 4 South American countries reported that Hib meningitis rates were similar 6–10 years after introduction of the vaccine in countries where booster doses were used and in those where boosters were not used.
key_data_points: Impact/effectiveness: >90% declines in invasive Hib disease after introduction in national immunization programmes
Outcome: reduced nasopharyngeal Hib colonization (herd protection suggested)
Population/schedule note: older age at start may increase vaccine effectiveness (6 cohort studies; no numeric estimate provided)
Duration/impact: sustained reduction in meningitis in young children after 5 years of 3p+0 use (no numeric estimate provided)
Comparative impact: Hib meningitis rates similar 6–10 years post-introduction in 4 South American countries with vs without booster (no numeric estimate provided)
study_population: General populations in countries introducing Hib conjugate vaccines (including developing countries; evaluation includes 4 South American countries); children/infants targeted for routine immunization
